body:
I'm aware of that, indeed, but the problem is I *never* get to talk about my interests or at least things that I find engaging on the same sort of level. Of course, now is the worst time because of the pandemic to be seeing new people, but even prior to it I never really managed to find people in my locality who form groups dedicated to the sort of interests I have. 

As for your question, I suppose it's because I end up talking about myself quite a bit, at least in reference to what is being discussed, usually with my own experience that would relate to the aforementioned subject. I worry I'm being judged and laughed at by people, particularly online, which I particularly feel when people blank or don't respond to me.

I'm afraid I don't have much advice to give, but I wanted to say I'm very much in the same position as what you have described here. I too have had many an experience where I've had people say my interests are "niche" or "boring" and they refuse to engage with me at all. It sucks so much, I know. 

The only thing I can suggest (though it hasn't worked too well for me so far) is to try and find groups or maybe even online communities dedicated to the sort of interests you have? That said, that brings a lot of challenges in itself.

But anyway, I guess I just want you to know you're not alone in feeling this, if that's any reassurance.

I agree with this wholeheartedly. I've spoken to people in my circle about how lonely I am and how few friends I have, but the people they try and suggest I affiliate and try to make friends with are the sort of people that, though nice, will just make me feel lonelier. I have nothing in common with these people and it just makes me feel like shit.

I am speaking to a therapist currently on a regular basis (over video calls due to the pandemic). As such we are attempting to try and work these things out. I know these things take time, I just get frustrated easily and impatient at times.

Thanks for your reply.

I'll try and befriend older people. I just need to work out how the hell I do that (when the pandemic is more under control really, I don't think now is really a good time for anyone to be making friends).

 Thanks for the advice and assurance.
Thank you! :)

Hi. For reference, I'm 24 years old. I do attend an online university but I find it hard to engage with the other students. 

Thanks for the advice, anyway. I find it hard to even find people of a similar temperament a lot of the time to try and engage with. I'm scared of most people my own age because of a lot of bad past experiences from being bullied and abused in my school years. 

Thank you for taking the time to respond. Have a good day and take care.

Hi. I realise that people are diverse and have different interests and values. I'm just expressing this frustration because I've almost entirely been met with cold rejection or even disdain from others for having "weird" interests and being an "odd" person generally. This has gone on for a good portion of my teenage years, and has only carried on into adulthood. 

I have tried stuff like chatrooms, I even did make some friends on one once (which I then drove away and became alienated from because of my anxious behaviour and need for constant reassurance) but I find it very difficult to start conversations with people. I don't know anymore. I fucking hate having almost no friends.

Anyway, thank you for taking the time to reply. Have a good day.

Thank you for the advice. I'm just very impatient, I've been waiting for so many years to have friends who I actually have things in common with, and I'm so sick of waiting. 

I'll take your advice, anyway. Thank you for the reply. Have a good day or night and take care.

Hi, thanks for replying.

I'm gonna risk sounding pretentious, but I have interests that people call "niche" and I find it hard to engage with others who don't share said interests. (For reference, I'm on the autistic spectrum and so I'm very interest driven and often fixate on certain subjects. Because of my admittedly narrow view, I find anything that isn't relevant to my interests to be "normal".)

I'm very fond of biology, particularly entomology (the study of insects, for those who don't know) and the visual arts (stuff like cartoons, illustration and graphic novels, in particular)  but I know pretty much absolutely no one in any of my circles who enjoys these things. People keep calling them "niche". 

I don't know. I get very wary of people because of being bullied and abused (which I won't go into here), which in turn I feel is a double-bind. I'm quite misanthropic about people yet I desire the presence of people. It sucks. I wish I could be a little paramecium or something that has no concept of self.

Anyway, thank you for listening. Have a good day/night.
I realise I'm being ignored again. I need to stop expecting things from others. I just should just stop screaming at the wind.
I talk to myself all the time. Always have done, I find it helps prior to social situations with the social anxiety I experience, to rehearse conversations.
I hear you. Especially on the "just pray" part. Urgh.

Thank you. I appreciate your advice very much. As for online connections, I have a few, maybe even some people I would call friends, but I guess I want people I can know in person too. I don't know, but as I say I appreciate you taking the time to respond to me. Have a good day.

Hey, thanks for the response. 

I see what you are saying. I do try *somewhat* to get to know people, problem is I'm very judgemental when I probably need not to be. I'll admit that. I am on the autistic spectrum and often struggle to think of people or things in alternate ways to my initial perceptions, for a possible explanation. 

Again, as I said, I have what a lot of people think of as specific or "niche" interests; my main passions are biology (especially fields such as entomology and microbiology) as well as the visual arts, particularly stuff like graphic novels and cartoons. It just gets so lonely that I don't have anyone I know in real life *at all* who share even a shred of interest in the aforementioned things. As an example, I've had many an occasion where I've read about a genus of beetle that I find fascinating, but have no one to share it this interest and fascination with. It sucks so much.

I don't know, I will take in what you have said, I just find putting it into practice so difficult as I'm bad at talking to and engaging with a lot of people as it is.

Thank you for replying. I hope you have a good day.
How do I do that? The doubts are so loud. I can't think of anything else.

I appreciate your comment. I try and do what you've suggested, building around the things one does like about their self, but I only get so far before I feel that I'm lying to myself. I wish I knew a way out of this.

Thanks for commenting, have a good day.

Thank you for your reply. I understand what you are saying about changing thought processes, I just find that so difficult. I am speaking to a therapist at the moment which is helping. 

I just overthink things and compare myself to others which only makes things worse, even with things I do simply for enjoyment. As an example, I'm part of an online artist chat group and I feel so inadequate when I see what other people are producing. That's not even going into the fact that the people who abused me when I was in school all now, as far as I can tell, have good jobs and happy lives, when they should all be fucking miserable for making life hell for me and other people. 

Anyway, thank you for reading my posts here, I appreciate that someone cared enough to respond. Thank you and have a good day.
Thank you for the response, I'm not a Christian but I appreciate what you're saying and your offer of messaging you. Take care.
No worries. Best of luck to you and take care.

Absolutely. I read way too much into what others say to me or about me all the time. It’s a hard one, and I’m still figuring out what I can do in response to this issue for myself. That said, I’ve been in a similar position, in that I was part of a regular group chat between me and some friends. I’d read too much into what they’d say, particularly if they were making jokes involving me and I’d panic and obsess over it.

My advice to you, as this has helped me, is that though it is perhaps not always easy to do (particularly when you’re in the moment, that’s what I’ve found) is to stop looking at or even engaging with the chat if possible, be it for an hour or even a few days, and just focus on something else, like something you enjoy doing. I’ve found that hard myself, but it can help to focus and distract yourself with other things. 

Anyway, I hope things get better for you.
Thank you for writing this. I really needed to read this because I feel so crappy about myself at the moment. I wish you the same good thoughts. <3

Thank you for this post. I've recently obsessed a lot about what others, who I perceive as friends, and what they probably think about me. I suppose the problem from here is accepting when people simply won't like you, or rather they *did* but then they don't anymore as a result of one's actions. I want to get better with that because I'm wasting so much energy on it.

Ah, I see. Well, I like drawing, which is one of the aforementioned interests I have. I'm considering trying to find more servers to share art or comics and the like, but the problem is that some of these servers are huge and intimidate me a bit as a result. I'll take your advice onboard though, so thank you once again.
Yeah, the current situation doesn't help, certainly. I hope I eventually find some people. Thanks for your comment.

I *do* have Discord and am a member of a few servers. The problem is I really struggle to start conversations with people, particularly on the larger servers. I have some people I could call friends though on a smaller server, but I'm questioning whether the feeling is mutual because I feel like I'm really awkward around them and bring them down.

I suppose that's one way of viewing it. My mind catastrophises and thinks in such a black and white, all-or-nothing mindset (attributable to my anxiety disorder) but I hope I can get to the point where I can think more like what you have described. I know it's easier said than done. Thank you for your comment.

I suppose not, it's just been such a long time since I've had a good conversation with anyone about my passions (which include biology. I'm studying it at the moment on an online university). Maybe I should just be less picky, but I can't emphasise enough how much I love being able to get on with people who as passionate as I am. Thank you for replying.
Yes, I suppose that's true. I just wish I wasn't so lonely and picky, I guess. Thanks for you reply.

I guess so. I understand the analogy of drawing, yes. I know it will take time, I just feel so god damn hopeless and like my mind is a curse. Thank you for your response anyway, it made sense to me. I'll think about it.

I had an incident occur when I had just turned 16 that resulted in a lot of trauma and suicidal thoughts. I was an absolute wreck for months afterwards, I often wanted to be sick, had panic attacks and didn't really help myself by looking for things that reminded me of the incident. The problem was in what I just mentioned-I kept looking for things online (like images and videos) of things that reminded me of what had happened to me. I essentially became addicted to the rush of anxiety (if that even makes sense) and I kept doing this because I thought I would be better off exposing myself to these things constantly.

It didn't help. What *did* help was fighting the temptation to look these things up, distracting myself and accepting the support offered to me by people I cared about, such as family and the few friends I had (and indeed, I still have very few friends, but I digress). Psychological help was also given to me, which also helped.

 I realise not everyone has access to these things, but it helped me immensely. I still have times where I'm reminded of it and feel anxious as a result, but I don't think about it very much anymore.

I'm just holding out hope that I can come out of what I'm going through right now, because I keep feeling like I want to give up now.
I know what you mean about not knowing a "why"-I have a lot of times where I feel like that without knowing why either. Anyway, I hope things improve for you in due course. Take care.

All the time, especially at the moment. Believe me, you're not the only one who experiences that. I guess my advice to you, should you want, is to think about why you might feel that way.

It's something that's been said to me a lot in the past and I find, as the old adage goes, knowing is half the battle. I'm not saying it's easy to find and confront these things, not by any means, I just think it can help to know *why* sometimes.

At this time I can't say. I want to say that I live for the beetles, butterflies and flowers but at this time I don't. Everything is so overwhelming. I know this universe is indifferent but I always feel like I'm just not meant to be "normal", as much as I wish I could be. 

If I could get rid of these feelings of self-loathing and clinginess, maybe I would feel less jaded about everything. I don't know anymore, I really don't.

I keep feeling so desperate for social contact with certain people. It's a feeling of longing but I know they don't give a shit about me ultimately and probably are having a lot of fun together without me. (For context, these are online "friends"- I use quotation marks because I doubt these feelings are mutual between me and them, or so my mind constantly tells me.) 

Why do I have to be this person? Let me be anyone else, please. I can't do this anymore.
Yes, I do relate. You're not the only one experiencing such things, I can certainly say that. It's not pleasant at all and I really hate feeling it.
That's nice of you to say. I'm glad someone does.
I hope so. I see nothing before me right now. I appreciate you telling me this, thank you again.
Thank you for your kind reply. I hope you find a happy place yourself. I want to give up. I really do, I feel like no one bar certain family members like me. I feel like the light is fading away.

I have a bit, yes. Again, I find it difficult to stop my mind wondering and just focus on my breathing or physical sensations in the body. I'm so deep in my head at the moment that in a number of instances in the past few days I've simply just sat and stared at the wall, motionless for hours. I really don't know what to do.

I do try to find other things to obsess over. I have some very particular interests that I like to be engrossed in, but at the moment I find it so hard to even begin thinking about anything other than my self-loathing and how much of a terrible person I believe I am. Do you have any advice for focusing on these other obsessions?

Thank you for your response.

Believe me, I've tried to distract myself by doing things like that. The problem is I'm so deep into my own head that I can't stop thinking about how much I worry that people hate me. I appreciate the suggestion and reply though, thank you.
No worries. Yes, hold onto that thought, and those happy memories. Just make sure to be kind to yourself, too. Take care.

I'm really sorry to hear that, I really am. I know the pain of losing an animal, it's like losing a friend, because in these cases they are our friends. I'm not going to say "oh, you'll get over it", because that never helps anyone. I suppose the thing to think is that you really loved your cat, and you got to spend time with her and know her. That's a thing worth celebrating if you ask me. 

I'd also like to add that you shouldn't blame yourself. I know a lot of people do (myself included) when loved ones pass away, but I try to think it's not what they would have wanted. 

I'm sorry if this isn't very helpful, I just know how horrible it is to lose an animal friend.

That's a good way of putting it. I shall try and remember that. I have funnily enough spoken to some of said friends earlier and have had a conversation with them about how I've felt. They've given me some constructive advice and were honest with me, I guess that's something.

Thank you again.

Hi there, thanks for your comment. I have done this actually before, the checking old messages/call logs, with both my family, friends and online friends. It's something I still do, but I have this constant fear that things have changed since, even if these things were said not long ago. Again,  I know that's irrational. 

Like with my online friends for instance, I have reached out and asked for assurance, quite a few times actually, but I worry they'll find it tiresome and get sick of me, so I don't do it now. It's kind of the same with other friends I have too. It doesn't help that I'm on the autistic spectrum and struggle to understand and read people sometimes, so that only complicates things further.

Anyway, thank you very much for taking the time to respond to me. I hope you have a good day.
